text:
Paula Mendes: We need to nail how LTS shows up in Console for version pinning. Specifically: labels, warnings, default selection, and linkouts to LTS release notes/known issues. What’s feasible for pilot vs GA?

Marissa Cole: +1. For the pilot I mostly want: 1) customers can *see* they’re on an LTS runtime, 2) they can pin to a specific LTS patch, 3) release notes link is one click. Fancy UX can wait.

Connor O'Brien: From Release Eng side: please don’t imply “auto-updates” unless we’re actually doing it. The first LTS patch is `1.18.1-lts` and we expect monthly patches. Customers will ask “am I tracking 1.18-lts and you roll me forward?” vs “am I pinned”. We should be explicit.

Paula Mendes: Agree. Current Console pattern for “runtime version” is a dropdown + “latest” tag. Could we do something like:
- Dropdown shows `1.18.1-lts` with an `LTS` pill
- Non-LTS versions show `Latest` (or nothing)
- Add a small callout under the selector: “LTS: slower-change channel, security + critical fixes only”

Bruno Silva: For Private: Console doesn’t actually control runtime version today (Helm/installer values do). We can show it as “Detected runtime version” and add link to docs.

Vivek Kulkarni: For Dedicated + Hosted, we can control selection. For Private, yeah, read-only plus guidance.

Rachel Kim: From CS POV: the biggest support issue is confusion. If a customer is on LTS, I want it obvious in the environment overview header, not buried in some settings page.

Marissa Cole: Can we do a banner at top of Environment page like: “Runtime channel: LTS (1.18.1-lts)” and make it clickable to release notes?

Paula Mendes: Banner is doable. We already have “Compute: Dedicated” tag area; we can add another tag row. Minimal work.

Elliot Price: Re release notes link: for LTS we’re planning a stable URL per patch (generated). If Console can just link to `/release-notes/runtime/1.18.1-lts` that’s ideal. For known issues: we can link to the “Runtime LTS known issues” doc for now.

Connor O'Brien: Re: naming. Please avoid “stable” as a synonym. We should call it exactly “LTS” and define it once.

Soojin Lee: +1 on consistent language. Marketing wants “Long Term Support (LTS) channel” and then “LTS patch releases” in notes.

Paula Mendes: Ok. Default selection question: should new envs default to LTS or Latest?

Marissa Cole: For self-serve Hosted, default should stay Latest. For enterprise Dedicated where they asked for LTS, we can default to LTS *if the org has LTS enabled*.

Rachel Kim: +100. Some customers explicitly don’t want LTS because they want faster model support. If we default everyone to LTS, we’ll create churn.

Vivek Kulkarni: Technically we can gate the “LTS” options behind a feature flag / entitlement (org-level). So default stays Latest unless flag is on.

Connor O'Brien: Also: if LTS isn’t enabled, we shouldn’t show “LTS” options at all. Otherwise we’ll get “where is my LTS support window?” questions.

Paula Mendes: Makes sense. Proposed pilot UX:
1) Runtime Version selector shows available versions.
2) LTS versions have an `LTS` pill.
3) If org is LTS-entitled, show a filter toggle: `Show: Latest | LTS` (or just group headings).
4) When LTS selected, show warning text: “LTS receives security + critical fixes; features land on Latest first. Patch cadence monthly + out-of-band security fixes.”
5) Add “View release notes” link next to selected version.

Marissa Cole: Slight tweak: keep the selector simple. Group headings might be enough:
- “LTS channel” group (only if entitled)
- “Latest channel” group
No extra toggle.

Bruno Silva: +1. Dropdown grouping is straightforward.

Elliot Price: Please also add a link to “Upgrade + rollback guidance” when LTS is selected. Even if it’s a docs page for now.

Paula Mendes: Where would that live? Under the warning block?

Elliot Price: Yeah. Something like:
- View release notes
- Upgrade/rollback guide
- Known issues

Connor O'Brien: One more thing: we should surface whether it’s “pinned”. E.g., “Pinned to 1.18.1-lts”. Otherwise customers assume they’re floating.

Paula Mendes: Good call. Copy suggestion:
“Pinned runtime: 1.18.1-lts (LTS)”
And if they switch versions, confirmation modal says “You are changing pinned runtime version”.

Marissa Cole: Confirmation modal is good. We should also mention that downgrades may require rollback steps.

Vivek Kulkarni: For Hosted/Dedicated we can usually roll back quickly, but we still want to set expectation.

Rachel Kim: For Support, can we also display the release notes URL in the “Copy diagnostics” panel? People paste that into tickets.

Paula Mendes: Nice-to-have. Might be v2, but I can add “Runtime version” + “Channel” to the diagnostics payload.

Soojin Lee: Also, can we add a small “What is LTS?” tooltip to the LTS pill? Like hover shows 2 sentences.

Paula Mendes: Tooltip is cheap.

Connor O'Brien: Re short-term feasibility: everything above is fine, just please don’t promise “6-12 months support” in the UI itself. That belongs in docs because windows vary per branch.

Elliot Price: Agree. Console can say “Long Term Support channel” and link to policy page that has the exact support window.

Marissa Cole: Decision summary (unless objections):
- Default to Latest unless org is LTS-entitled
- In environment header: show “Runtime channel: LTS” + pinned version
- In runtime version dropdown: group LTS versions (tag/pill) + Latest versions
- When LTS selected: warning block + 3 links (release notes, known issues, upgrade/rollback)
- For Private: show detected version as read-only + docs link (no selection)

Bruno Silva: Works. For Private I’ll need the doc link finalized so we don’t link to a draft that moves.

Elliot Price: I’ll provide stable doc URLs by EOD. Release notes URL pattern will be ready once the generator is merged; for pilot we can link to Confluence release notes page as interim.

Paula Mendes: Cool. I’ll open a Console ticket with these acceptance criteria and call out “no auto-update implication.”

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: If you want exact copy for the warning block, ping me and I’ll align it w/ the backport policy language.

Rachel Kim: Thanks all. Once we have screenshots, I’ll add to the pilot comms so customers know where to look.

Paula Mendes: :white_check_mark: I’ll post a mock in this thread tomorrow.
